messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the merge from PR #6789 we're seeing a clear perf regression in canary. Latency up ~30% p95 for short batches. Looks like the kernel-selection heuristic started preferring a new variant for seq<=64 and it's causing extra compiles + KV cache churn. logs/snippet below.

aj: Which commit / PR exactly? link pls.

maria: PR 6789 (github.com/redwood/infra/6789) — merge commit 0a1b2c3. Repro on canary: model=redwood-lite, seq=32, batch=4. p95 180ms -> 240ms after merge. p50 ~ unchanged.

cheng: Can you paste the compile storm lines? also any evidence of KV cache evictions? That pattern sounds like bad kernel flip -> different cache keys.

maria: pasted logs:
```
[2026-11-02T14:12:01Z] kernel_picker: picked k_variant_x (score 0.48) for model redwood-lite seq=32
[2026-11-02T14:12:01Z] compile: starting compile k_variant_x (cost_est 0.27)
[2026-11-02T14:12:01Z] kvcache: eviction triggered, evicted 24 entries (usage 88%)
[2026-11-02T14:12:02Z] compile: finished k_variant_x (120ms)
[2026-11-02T14:12:03Z] kernel_picker: picked k_variant_y (score 0.46) for seq=32
[2026-11-02T14:12:03Z] compile: starting compile k_variant_y
[2026-11-02T14:12:03Z] kvcache: eviction triggered, evicted 26 entries
```

sam: repro steps I'm using locally: `./scripts/run-local --model redwood-lite --seq 32 --batch 4 --load-profile canary` produced same compile churn. command to run perf-ci: `./ci/bench.sh --suite=short-seq --iter=50`

perf-ci-bot: [CI] perf/short-seq job #432 failed threshold: p95 regression +28% vs baseline (baseline build 0a1a2b). See: ci.redwood/test/432

aj: I'm going to bisect between the last-good tag (v2026-10-28) and 0a1b2c3. `git bisect start 0a1b2c3 v2026-10-28`

cheng: My theory: the heuristic weight vector flip in heuristics.py (the new feature that tries to trade compile-time for runtime) mis-evaluated short sequences. Quick mitigation: prefer fallback kernel for seq<=48 or keep previous ordering until autotune has a stable sample. Patch snippet: 
```python
# heuristics.py (quick hotfix)
if seq_len <= 48 and workload.batch_size <= 8:
    kernel_score['k_variant_old'] += 0.2
```

maria: Can we hold the canary rollout? Deploy looks like it's hitting ~12% of traffic. If we pause we can avoid customer impact. @deploy-bot canary pause? :pray:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused by request (maria). Current canary fraction frozen at 12%.

aj: Bisect results: bad commit is 0a1b2c3 -> change in heuristics.py line 143-170 where the new scoring func was introduced. Repro steps and bisect log attached. Conclusion: the scoring math pushed k_variant_x up for short seqs, but that kernel compiles slower and evicts KV entries because it uses different cache keys (we didn't normalize key prefix).

sam: Evidence of KV key divergence: grep from logs: 
```
kvcache: key_prefix mismatch: old=rlite/v1/kA new=rlite/v2/kB
kvcache: store key=rlite/v2/kB/slot_17
```
This explains the thrash.

cheng: I'll open a revert PR and a follow-up that does two things: (1) revert the scoring change, (2) add a unit test that asserts kernel selection stability for seq <= 64 across the last 3 heuristics versions. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/6798

aj: +1 to revert. If we want a faster mitigation we can also bump the score boost to the old kernel as a hotfix (cheng snippet). Which do we prefer? revert or quick score tweak?

maria: Revert is safer and clearer. Let's revert the heuristic change in canary now, then we can ship a more considered rework with tests. Can someone do the revert deploy?

cheng: I pushed revert branch `revert/heuristics-0a1b2c3` and opened PR 6798. Running quick CI.

perf-ci-bot: [CI] revert/heuristics-0a1b2c3 job #434 passed unit tests. perf suite queued.

aj: I'll promote the revert to canary once perf CI confirms.

sam: quick note for post-mortem: add an integration test exercising kvcache key stability when kernels change (we currently only test functional output). Also add a lightweight perf check for compile-time delta per kernel to prevent compile-heavy picks for tiny sequences.

maria: Thanks everyone. Plan: (1) keep canary paused, (2) merge revert PR 6798 after perf CI green, (3) roll to canary and monitor p95, (4) post-mortem + follow-up PR for tests + normalized kvcache keys. I'll file the incident ticket.

aj: update: perf CI for revert passed perf/short-seq with p95 within 2% of baseline. Merging revert now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout resumed with revert/heuristics-0a1b2c3 at 12% (manual). Monitor dashboards: https://console.redwood/ops/canary

maria: Canary looks stable after revert. p95 back to baseline. Closing thread after incident ticket created. Thanks :thumbsup:

(threads/notes: follow-up items -> add unit tests, kvcache normalization, telemetry on kernel compile times)
